title: Idempotent leading coefficient of a commuting idempotent determinant
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $J$ a finite set, and $T,P\in\operatorname{Mat}_J(A)$ with $P^2=P$ and $TP=PT$. Let $D(T,P)$ be the polynomial of [def-weil-pbc-idempotent-charpoly]. Its leading coefficient $c$ satisfies $c^2=c$.

source.place: Tag 09XI, lemma-characterize-henselian-pair, proof of (3) implies (1), splitting and characteristic-polynomial paragraphs; matrix formula and omitted details written out by G2

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-charpoly-local-charpoly] to obtain a finite standard cover and an identification of the localized determinant with a matrix characteristic polynomial on each cover member.

The localized polynomial is monic by Matrix.charpoly_monic from [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module-properties]. Put d=natDegree of the global determinant and e=natDegree of its localized polynomial. Polynomial.natDegree_map_le gives e<=d. By coeff_map and coeff_natDegree, the localized image of the global leading coefficient is the local coefficient at d. It is zero if e<d and one if e=d. These equations also hold in zero localizations without a Nontrivial assumption. Thus the localized image of the original leading coefficient is idempotent.

Apply Module.eq_zero_of_isLocalized_span from [lem-weil-pbc-localized-span-eq-zero] to c*c-c, with c the global leading coefficient and with A viewed as a module over itself. Each local image is zero by the coefficient calculation. Hence c*c-c=0 and c*c=c.

theorem isIdempotentElem_idempotentCharpoly_leadingCoeff
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {n : Type v} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (T P : Matrix n n A) (hP : P * P = P) (hTP : T * P = P * T) :
    IsIdempotentElem (idempotentCharpoly T P).leadingCoeff
